original_question: Assume S is a normal surface whose singularities are du Val singularities. Is the Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(S) reduced for every d?
target_in_paper: Problem XIII in §2.2 ("Singular surfaces"). In the setting of Problem XII, the paper asks whether, if the singularities of S are du Val, the Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(S) is reduced for every d. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target: it has the right object (a normal surface S), the right singularity class (du Val singularities), the right moduli space (Hilb_d(S)), and the right property (reducedness for every d). It also correctly focuses on reducedness rather than irreducibility, which is important because the nearby context says irreducibility is already known in the du Val case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
missing_details: The paper’s standing convention is that everything is over an algebraically closed field k. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

In §2.2, the algebraic description of du Val singularities is stated over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, so characteristic 0 is part of the paper-faithful ambient setup. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
The paper defines Hilb_d(S) for quasi-projective schemes S, so adding quasi-projective makes the question fully stand-alone in the paper’s notation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

In §2.2, a "singularity" means the complete local ring at a singular point; thus saying that S has du Val singularities means that every complete local ring at a singular point is du Val. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
Hilb_d(S) should be unpacked as the Hilbert scheme of zero-dimensional subschemes of S of degree (length) d. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
The quantifier should be made explicit as: for every integer d ≥ 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

Reduced should be understood scheme-theoretically, not merely set-theoretically or topologically. This distinction matters because §2.2 separately records irreducibility for the du Val case and then asks for reducedness. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and let S be a normal quasi-projective surface over k such that for every singular point s in S, the complete local ring \hat{\mathcal{O}}_{S,s} is a du Val singularity. For each integer d \ge 1, is the Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(S) parametrizing zero-dimensional subschemes of S of degree d reduced?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem XIII in §2.2, so the right refinement is to make the paper’s hidden conventions explicit rather than broaden the problem. I therefore kept the question narrowly about reducedness of Hilb_d(S), added the ambient hypotheses from §1.3 (algebraically closed base field and the meaning of Hilb_d(S)), and added the local meaning of "singularity" and the characteristic-0 du Val context from §2.2. I did not replace the question by a broader neighboring problem such as irreducibility, since §2.2 explicitly says irreducibility is already known for normal surfaces whose singularities are du Val. The accessible HTML version does not expose exact in-article page numbers for these items, but external bibliographic snippets show that the published article occupies pp. 3–25 in Contemporary Mathematics 805. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
